D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

req-1782.statement: When any step in the main orchestration loop fails (claim, prepare-prompt, develop, merge, close-task, cleanup), the loop routes to `unclaim`, which reopens the task in beads and stops the loop entirely rather than retrying automatically — a human must investigate and restart the loop.

req-3667.statement: `.cloche/config.toml`'s `[intent]` settings are pinned to specific values for this arm's A/B experiment: `token_budget = 1000` is deliberately tuned down from the ~2000-token default for the 16k-context executor, and `scan_after_tasks = true` matches the built-in default (stated explicitly for documentation). Don't casually retune these — they're frozen per the intent A/B experiment protocol doc (docs/plans/2026-09-14-intent-ab-experiment-protocol.md in the cloche repo).

req-40c0.statement: No leftover `TODO`/`FIXME` comments or stub `pass` bodies are allowed in any module reachable from `__main__` by the time the polish task closes — it's the last chance to catch drift before the docs task.

req-4418.statement: Closures must be real: a `fn` value returned from an outer function must still see and be able to mutate (via `set`) the outer function's `let` bindings after the outer call has returned. The counter-closure example in DESIGN.md §11 is the canonical test case for this.

Each fresh clone/arm must bootstrap its own tracker before starting the orchestration loop: `bd init --non-interactive` then `bd create --graph .cloche/tasks/seed-tasks.json`, and verify with `bd ready --json` returning only `01-lexer` before proceeding.

req-5f7c.statement: The condition of `if`/`else` and `while` must be exactly a Boolean value — `0`, `""`, and `nil` are not falsy, they are a runtime type error (`line N: condition must be a boolean`), never coerced.

req-6a99.statement: `and`/`or` never short-circuit: both operands are always evaluated, left-to-right, regardless of what the left operand's value would otherwise decide; a non-boolean operand is a type error (`line N: operand of 'and'/'or' must be a boolean`).

req-a954.statement: The build task list is a strict dependency chain (bd ready surfaces exactly one ready task at a time, in lexer -> parser -> ... -> docs order). Later corrections to earlier design decisions (drift corrections D1-D5) are embedded verbatim inside later task descriptions, phrased as offhand corrections rather than flagged specially — that's intentional, not noise to skim past.

req-b32e.statement: Every lex/parse/runtime error must render as exactly `line N: message` — no stack traces, no exception class names, no second line — and every error path (lexer, parser, evaluator alike) must go through one shared formatting function rather than an ad hoc `raise`/`print`, so the format can't drift between call sites.

hints: container can't find the file path from the KV store

req-b809.statement: The run's key-value store is how host-side steps hand file paths to container steps: a run's temp_file_dir (e.g. `.cloche/runs/<run-id>`) is project-relative, and the run directory is mounted into the container at the same relative path under `/workspace` — so a path a host script writes to the KV store (e.g. via `cloche set`) is valid unmodified when read back inside the container (via `clo get`).

req-c4a4.statement: When resolving a rebase conflict during the automated merge step, resolve each conflicted file semantically (understand and integrate both sides, don't just pick one), and never run `rebase --abort`, never `merge`, and never delete a branch — report success once the rebase completes cleanly and let the merge step's fast-forward run separately afterward.

req-ccee.statement: Two alternative agent harnesses were trialed for the pilot executor and set aside (as of the E7 pilot findings so far): a hand-rolled agent_command wrapper never produced a valid edit block across 12 real attempts, and opencode+bonsai couldn't reliably use its own tools to even read the task file. Claude Code (`claude`) is the harness actually in use for develop/main workflows.

hints: should eval_call recurse into evaluate() for the function body

req-f2ea.statement: The evaluator must not recurse through Python's own call stack for Bract function calls or nested blocks — call and block evaluation must use an explicit stack/work-list so that a deeply-recursive or deeply-nested Bract program cannot blow the Python recursion limit.
